Threat Model Name: Water Treatment Plant - OT Threat Model (example)

Owner: John Desilva

Reviewer:

Contributors: John Desilva

Description: Municipal water treatment plant: SCADA server and control-room HMI supervise a chemical dosing PLC (chlorine analyzer, dosing pump drive) and a filtration PLC. An engineering workstation programs the PLCs. Process data is stored in a historian and replicated to a DMZ historian for corporate reporting. The vendor connects through a remote access gateway. Remote lift stations are controlled over DNP3 via cellular routers.

Assumptions: Example model. Field devices (Level 0) are shown only where they carry digital data. The plant network is wired Ethernet; remote lift stations use a public cellular network.

External Dependencies: Cellular carrier; vendor remote support; corporate IT network.

Category:Tampering
Description:An attacker could force inputs or outputs, or overwrite the I/O image, so Chemical Dosing PLC acts on false values or drives outputs directly.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Restrict force and I/O override functions to authorised engineering roles. Show active forces on the HMI. Log and alarm on force events.

Category:Spoofing

Justification:<no mitigation provided>

8. Adversary-in-the-middle tampering of SCADA Server to Chemical Dosing PLC traffic  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:Traffic between SCADA Server and Chemical Dosing PLC crosses a trust boundary without integrity protection, so an attacker in the path could modify values, commands or responses without detection.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Use protocol security with message integrity (OPC UA Sign/SignAndEncrypt, CIP Security, DNP3-SA, IEC 62351, TLS). Where the protocol cannot be secured, tunnel it through an authenticated, integrity-protected conduit (IPsec/TLS) and restrict paths at the zone boundary.
IEC 62443-4-1 Practice:SD - Secure by design

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Traffic between SCADA Server and Chemical Dosing PLC is not encrypted across the trust boundary. An attacker could capture process values, tag names, program contents or credentials and use them to plan an attack.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Encrypt flows that cross zone boundaries where confidentiality is required (TLS, OPC UA SignAndEncrypt, IPsec tunnels). Classify data to decide where encryption is needed. Do not send credentials over unencrypted channels.

261. Command, trip or alarm messages between Remote Access Gateway and Engineering Workstation blocked  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An attacker on the path, or on a device in between, could selectively drop or delay commands, trips, alarms or status messages between Remote Access Gateway and Engineering Workstation while the link still looks healthy, so a response to a process upset never arrives.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Use communication watchdogs, heartbeats and sequence counters so that missing or late messages are detected (CR 3.1, CR 7.1). Define the safe state on loss of communication (CR 3.6). Alarm on communication loss to the operator. Use redundant paths for essential functions and keep safety trips independent of the control network.

341. Local audit trail on Remote Access Gateway lost, overwritten or cleared  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Embedded and network devices often keep only a small local event buffer. An attacker could clear it, flood it until older events are overwritten, or reboot Remote Access Gateway so evidence held in volatile memory is lost.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Protect audit records against deletion (CR 3.9) and keep them across restarts. Forward events in near real time to a central collector (CR 6.1, syslog over TLS). Warn when audit capacity is nearly used (CR 2.9). Record clearing of the log as an audit event itself.
